nodes.label: API reference index (autosummary)
nodes.rationale: One page per public module generated from docstrings; the docstrings are the point because they cite ticket IDs, explain why a default is what it is, and record decisions.

nodes.label: Why pyquant.config gets a hand-built page
nodes.rationale: pydantic v2 moves model fields off the class at class-creation time, so plain autodoc renders each one as a bare name: type with neither its default nor the comment explaining it.

nodes.label: Documented layer map (config/data/models/analysis/cli/api)
nodes.rationale: models/tft.py is the only module besides data/dataset.py that imports pytorch-forecasting or Lightning; analysis/ is library-agnostic (plain numpy arrays and dataclasses, no torch, no Typer, no Rich); cli/ is a thin caller; api/ is a second front-end over the same layers.

nodes.label: Intersphinx upstream type resolution
nodes.rationale: This codebase is largely a thin, correct layer over pandas/numpy/torch/pytorch_forecasting/pydantic, so knowing exactly which TimeSeriesDataSet or DataFrame a function returns carries real explanatory weight. Runtime type objects stringify to their defining module (pandas.core.frame.DataFrame) rather than the documented public name, so conf.py maps the former onto the latter before giving up.

nodes.label: nitpicky is deliberately off (PYQ-233)
nodes.rationale: Turning it on would make every unresolvable type reference an error, but a large share of remaining unresolved names are upstream types whose inventories do not publish them - noisy rather than informative. The build already runs under -W --keep-going, so a broken cross-reference in this project's own docstrings fails the build today.

nodes.label: Private helpers omitted from the reference
nodes.rationale: _prediction_dataset, _evaluate_validation, _window_validation_dataset and friends carry some of the densest reasoning in the codebase; read them in the source or via the [source] links on each page.
